M30-004-0244.summary: Delacroix tells Létombe that the consuls at New York and Boston have sent him President Adams's speech at the opening of the extraordinary session, that he hopes the President does not mean to go to extremes, and that the Directory's position is in his despatch of 29 prairial. He asks for prompt detail on Congress, and orders that consuls keep political matter out of clear despatches, pass it to the agents charged with politics or put it in cipher, since what has already been intercepted must serve as a lesson.
M30-004-0244.en:
Heading in clear on the copy: The Minister of External Relations to Citizen Létombe, Consul at Philadelphia, acting
provisionally as Consul General of the French Republic in the United States.

The Consuls at New York and Boston, Citizen, have sent me the speech made by <<Mr>> Adams at the opening of the
extraordinary [session]. I await with much impatience your own despatches, which will no doubt bring me the decision
of the federal government. Despite the tone of Mr Adams's speech, and that of the draft address of the House of
Representatives, I hope that the President of the United States does not seriously mean to go to extremes. As for
the Directory's sentiments, they are set out in my despatch of 29 prairial, and I have [nothing] to add to it.
